notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/03/2025
Patient: Yon Cassin, 70 y/o F

Attended PSG 04/03/2025. Study revealed severe sleep-disordered breathing. AHI 51.8/h. CA+MA 4% of total AHI. O2 sat nadir 82%. Sleep efficiency 78%. REM latency 90 min. Periodic limb movements within normal limits. No significant arrhythmias noted. Recommend CPAP titration given severity of apnea.

notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/29/2026
Patient: Yon Cassin, 71 y/o F

Hx: OSA dx 2018, CPAP started 2019. Pt reports poor adherence.

CPAP dl avg 1.7 h/night, 37% nights despite mask refit; SDM w/ pt: CPAP intolerant.

Exam: BMI 29, no nasal obstruction noted.

Plan: Discussed alternative therapies including oral appliance and positional therapy. Will consider referral for upper airway stimulation evaluation. Follow-up in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Counseled on sleep hygiene and weight management.

Otolaryngology Consultation
Date: 09/15/2026
Patient: Yon Cassin, 71yo F

71yo W referred for HGNS eval. PMH notable for OSA, CPAP intolerant. Exam: Tonsils 1+, no other obstruction. Nasal passages patent. Oral cavity unremarkable. DISE 08/28/2026: AP velum collapse, no CCC. Hypopharynx and tongue base stable. No significant lateral wall collapse.

Plan: Proceed with HGNS candidacy workup. Discussed risks/benefits with patient. Follow-up scheduled post-implant evaluation.
